svg.title: MicroLogix Lockout kill chain - US water utility PLC reconfiguration, July-August 2026
svg.desc: Two-lane diagram. The left lane follows a victim water utility: an internet-facing MicroLogix 1100 or 1400 controller reachable on EtherNet/IP over a cellular link; an unauthenticated List Identity read that fingerprints the fleet; the critical controller password change and IP address rewrite that seize device identity and cause loss of view; project upload and ladder logic modification; the critical physical consequence of pressure loss, flooding and disabled well and treatment controls at Braham and Plymouth Minnesota; and recovery through manual operation, factory reset per Rockwell advisory SD1790 and a validated program restore. The right lane holds the actor side enabling conditions: internet wide scanning of engineering ports, the cellular carrier path that bypasses every IT control, the critical reuse of one integrator network design across many utilities, end of life hardware with no patch path, underground circulation of engineering knowledge, and adjacent pro Russia hacktivist claims against Canadian water systems. Detection anchors are the external EtherNet/IP session and the CIP write that changes controller identity or program, both marked by cross lane arrows.
svg.text: MicroLogix Lockout - reconfiguration of exposed PLCs at US water utilities
Vendors: FBI/EPA + CISA + Forescout Vedere Labs + LevelBlue SpiderLabs - Dates: 2026-07-30 / 2026-08-04 / 2026-08-05 - Cluster: unattributed - Day 108
VICTIM WATER UTILITY - controller, process and recovery
ENABLING CONDITIONS - exposure, access path and supply
Internet-facing controller on cellular WAN
MicroLogix 1100 / 1400 at wells, towers, lift stations
EtherNet/IP answers on TCP 44818, no authentication
T1133 / T0886 - path never crosses the IT perimeter
Vendor ID: Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley
Unauthenticated identity read
List Identity returns vendor, product, firmware, serial
Fleet triaged from the banner alone, no process touched
T1595.002 / T0888 - reconnaissance is free here
4407 devices on 44818 (Shodan, 2026-08-03)
22 of them in cities that reported incidents
Controller password set or changed (critical)
Operators can no longer go online with RSLogix 500
Legitimate configuration write, no payload, no file
T1531 / T0812 / T0859 - identity seized
Recovery only via factory reset (SD1790)
Default or absent password was the precondition
Controller IP address rewritten (critical)
SCADA and HMI polling breaks instantly
Device disappears from the process graph
T0836 / T0829 - loss of view
No endpoint telemetry survives this point
Firewall and carrier flow logs are the evidence
Project upload and logic modification
Program pulled from the controller, then written back
Ladder-logic discrepancies noticed across several sites
T0845 / T0843 / T0889 - modify program
Artifacts: *.RSS *.SLC *.ACD *.L5K *.L5X
AA26-097A line also altered Add-On Instructions
Physical consequence (critical)
Wells, treatment plant, towers and lift stations
Pressure loss, flooding, boil-water notices
T0855 / T0827 / T0826 / T0879 - loss of control
Braham MN: well and plant controls disabled
Plymouth MN: 2 towers + 14 lift stations offline
Manual operation and validated restore
Plant runs on documented manual procedure
Factory reset, then re-download a known-good project
Validate the backup before restoring it
Rockwell advisory SD1790 is the recovery path
Key switch back to RUN only after a rung-level diff
A
Internet-wide scanning of engineering ports
TCP 44818, 502, 102 and UDP 2222 swept continuously
EtherNet/IP is the second most attacked OT protocol
No exploit needed - the protocol answers by design
Exposure fell 47% since March 2020 (7814 -> 4169)
B
Cellular carrier path as the access layer
Over 70% of US exposed controllers on mobile networks
Field modems place OT assets outside every IT control
No EDR, no identity provider, no enterprise firewall
Private APN or ZTNA is the only structural fix
19 of 22 hosts in affected cities on one carrier
Sierra Wireless ACEmanager exposed on tcp/9191
C
Shared integrator design multiplies success (critical)
FBI: similar third-party configurations across victims
One working method reproduced against many utilities
Eagan MN: 15 controllers, adjacent addresses
Similar serials, uniform firmware, one GPS pair
Compromise the template, compromise every customer
Vendor config audit belongs in the threat model
D
End-of-life hardware, no patch path
MicroLogix 1100 discontinued on 2022-04-30
Weak authentication, logging and access control
CVE-2017-16740 fits 19 of 22 hosts by firmware
Modbus TCP precondition never confirmed
CVE-2021-22681 on KEV does NOT affect MicroLogix
No CVE confirmed as the vector of this campaign
E
Engineering knowledge from underground supply
RSLogix 500 / 5000 courses and manuals circulated
Project archives, HMI screenshots, network diagrams
Lowers the barrier below ICS-malware capability
Legitimate tooling is all the actor ever needed
Studio 5000, EcoStruxure, TIA Portal in AA26-097A
Leased third-party infrastructure for the sessions
F
Adjacent hacktivist claims, same exposure
NoName057(16): Ontario water system, 2026-07-23
Z-Pentest: Saint-Noel QC drinking water, confirmed
Screenshot-driven publicity, lower capability
Same pool of exposed HMIs and weak remote access
Attribution of the US wave remains unresolved
Iran-nexus is a hypothesis, not a conclusion
Durable detection anchors
1) accepted inbound flow to tcp/44818, 502, 102 or udp/2222 from a non-allowlisted source 2) CIP write that changes controller identity
3) program checksum drift against the approved offline baseline 4) gateway admin login, config export or firmware change on the access path
No CVE confirmed as the vector - exposure and weak controller authentication were the vulnerability; KEV entry CVE-2021-22681 does not affect MicroLogix
